subject: MAP Close Playbook — acceptance criteria + rollback triggers
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@averyhealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: MAP Close Playbook — acceptance criteria + rollback triggers

Emily — great to meet earlier. Per our call, I’m sending a first-pass MAP and an acceptance-test checklist to align on what ‘success’ looks like for the evaluation and the close timeline. Attached: MAP-draft-v1.xlsx (mutual action plan) and acceptance-tests-v1.md (detailed test cases).

High-level proposal (summary):
- Evaluation window: 4 weeks (pilot cadence we discussed)
- Success definition: 3 primary signals must pass for go decision —
  1) Production-congruent latency: 95th percentile < 450ms on your peak test profile
  2) Response quality: >= 92% pass rate on our labelled prompt set (concordance > 0.92)
  3) Throughput: sustained 120rps with autoscale profile in Dedicated mode
- Exit gates: must have no Severity-1 regressions in the last 72 hours and operational runbook validated with on-call contact
- Acceptance tests: smoke, load, quality, and failover (listed in acceptance-tests-v1.md)
- Rollback/failback rules: If any gate fails twice in the same week, we trigger a rollback to the prior model variant and invoke a 48-hour remediation window.

As next steps I suggest: you review the attached MAP and mark any adjustments to the success thresholds; we’ll lock the MAP and then schedule a joint kickoff (30–45 min) to confirm roles and timeline.

If you want, I can add procurement contact into the MAP so we can parallelize contract steps with the pilot.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0192 | dylan.brooks@redwood.com

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), acceptance-tests-v1.md (markdown)

From: Emily Park <emily.park@averyhealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Torres <sam.torres@averyhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP Close Playbook — acceptance criteria + rollback triggers

Thanks Dylan — this is helpful and a good starting point. A few quick notes from product and procurement: 

Product feedback:
- Latency: 450ms p95 is reasonable, but can we split tests by short vs long context? Our long-context flows (12k tokens) are the biggest risk — can you add a separate p95 target for >6k token requests?
- Quality: instead of a single 92% threshold, can we have pass thresholds per intent bucket (Triage, Summarize, Recommend)? We’ll send a short sample set for each.

Procurement (Sam):
- Include standard procurement timelines: we’ll need a 30-day review for T&C and a single redline pass. Sam, I’ll handoff any contract questions to Dylan after we finalize the MAP.

Also — can you add an explicit data-retention acceptance test (audit log availability for 90 days) so our security team can sign off in parallel?

I’ll pull the sample prompts and attach the intent buckets by EOD tomorrow. Once we align, let’s lock the MAP and the kickoff.

—Emily Park
Senior Product Manager, Avery Health
emily.park@averyhealth.com

Emily / Sam — thanks for the quick read and the product asks. I’ve updated the MAP and the acceptance-tests doc to incorporate your requests; attaching a slimmed acceptance-tests-v1.md and a one-page runbook PDF (mutual-action-timeline.pdf) that maps who owns what and when. Key updates below: 

What changed (summary):
- Latency: added split targets:
  • Short-context (<= 1k tokens): p95 < 350ms
  • Long-context (> 6k tokens): p95 < 1.2s (measured with our long-run harness)
- Quality: pass thresholds by intent bucket (Triage >= 90%, Summarize >= 94%, Recommend >= 88%); see table in acceptance-tests-v1.md
- Data retention: audit logs available for 90 days and retrievable via secure link; we added an evidence checklist for security to validate during week 1 smoke tests
- Rollback: clarified triggers — any S1 or two failed gate runs in 7 days => immediate rollback + 48h remediation; critical fixes follow a triage board with Ben as incident owner

Proposed cadence / timeline: 
- Week 0 (prep): finalize MAP and sign mutual-action items (procurement parallelized)
- Week 1 (smoke + security): basic functionality, audit log check, and quality baseline
- Week 2 (load): throughput and burst tests with autoscale profile
- Week 3 (long-context & edgecases): long request scenarios and latency profiling
- Week 4 (stabilize & signoff): final pass and go/no-go meeting

Owner matrix (one-pager):
- Demo/validation owner: Dylan Brooks (sales lead)
- QA & test harness owner: Marissa Cole (solutions engineering)
- Incident owner: Ben Carter (support/ops)
- Procurement/contract owner: Sam Torres (Avery Health)

Next actions I’ll take:
1) Update Drive MAP link (done)
2) Add Sam as procurement contact in the MAP
3) Share a short checklist for Week 1 smoke tests (Marissa will own execution)

If that looks good I’ll circulate for final signoff and then we can lock the timeline.

Best —
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: acceptance-tests-v1.md (updated), mutual-action-timeline.pdf
